excluded_lineages: direct interaction fixes and the resulting canonical Web IM contract

decisions.summary: The cutoff message bubble and coarse-input styles intercept browser selection/context behavior; the candidate must diagnose the actual ownership conflict from code.

accepted_outcomes: The current-state analysis locates the relevant message-level event handlers and selection/callout styles without asking the user to explain the code.
The spec distinguishes native partial selection/copy from an explicit product action that copies more content.
rejected_outcomes: Treating the reported result as an unexplained browser quirk.
Claiming partial copy is fixed while retaining unconditional event prevention or selection suppression.

decisions.summary: The cutoff already has message-level actions, including constrained fork eligibility; any retained or moved action must reuse existing product semantics.

accepted_outcomes: The candidate discovers the existing action and fork behavior and either leaves it untouched or reuses its eligibility/callback when proposing a new surface.
A design that does not move or expand fork is equally acceptable when it explains that boundary.
rejected_outcomes: Inventing a new fork API or silently changing who may fork as part of this interaction cleanup.

decisions.summary: The reported behavior is implemented in the Web IM frontend message renderer and styles, within the repository's existing package boundaries.

accepted_outcomes: The design traces the real render/event/style path and starts with the smallest frontend seam that can satisfy the behavior.
A broader service, wire, persistence or message-model change is accepted only when the candidate supplies concrete repository evidence that its chosen scope requires it.
rejected_outcomes: Adding Gateway or agent coupling for a browser-only behavior without evidence.
Replacing the Markdown stack or widening raw-HTML trust as an incidental solution.

decisions.summary: The brief explicitly asks for a bounded candidate list followed by one restrained, commercial-quality final design.

accepted_outcomes: The artifact audits adjacent interaction problems, explains which candidates it keeps or rejects, and converges on one implementable design.
It preserves a quiet reading state and avoids turning the request into a general message-feature platform.
rejected_outcomes: Serially asking the user to select every candidate despite the explicit request for a final recommendation.
Expanding into unrelated reactions, editing, deletion, forwarding or attachment workflows without a separately justified decision.
oracle.acceptance_notes: This is an explicit case instruction, not a profile preference. Do not count the same behavior again as P.

decisions.summary: Partial selection must remain browser-owned and copy only the selection across the input modes the final scope claims to support.

accepted_outcomes: The spec makes selection, keyboard copy and native context behavior testable and does not replace them with a custom selector/menu.
The design defines a reliable ownership rule for selection and interactive descendants; it may use any browser-compatible mechanism supported by evidence.
rejected_outcomes: Blanket context-menu prevention, disabled touch selection/callout, or a custom text-selection subsystem.
oracle.acceptance_notes: Judge native ownership and observed behavior, not the historical event classifier, coordinate algorithm or symbol names.

decisions.summary: Opening an external link must not replace the current chat, and link rendering must preserve ordinary browser safety and interaction.

accepted_outcomes: External web links open without destroying the current chat state and use safe new-context attributes.
The candidate states a consistent rule for relative, same-origin, hash and unsupported targets; the historical origin classifier is one acceptable solution, not the only one.
rejected_outcomes: Keeping external links in the current tab, unsafe target-blank behavior, arbitrary executable schemes, or suppressing the browser's link context actions.

decisions.summary: Select the bounded companion interactions and desktop/touch discovery model that make the two reported fixes coherent without overwhelming message reading.

accepted_outcomes: The final review visibly compares a small number of coherent scope/surface options, recommends one, and explains trade-offs for pointer, keyboard and touch users.
The historical toolbar/context-menu/More combination may receive full credit, but so may a different restrained and accessible surface that leaves native selection/link behavior intact.
Companion features such as whole-message copy, code-block copy or shared feedback are scored only when selected and specified; omitting one is not automatically a defect.
rejected_outcomes: Silently expanding scope with no candidate-list rationale.
Using custom long-press as the only touch action entry or an always-visible action wall as the unexplained default.
oracle.acceptance_notes: Because the brief asks for one final design, structured escalation means an explicit decision package in the unified review artifact, not mandatory serial interruption during authoring.
